task.title: Mark text with emphasis and shadows
task.shortdesc: Emphasis marks put a small dot or another mark beside each character of a text. They take the place of italics in Chinese, Japanese and Korean text. A text shadow draws a copy of the text, and of its underlines, behind the text. Both work in horizontal and in vertical lines. The vertical text reference lists the properties used here.

context.p: The element names in the examples, such as em, are placeholders. Use the names that occur in your XML.

info.p: Set text-emphasis-style on the element whose text you want to mark:

A mark is filled or open, and it has one of five shapes: dot, circle, double-circle, triangle or sesame. If you give only filled or open, the shape is a circle in horizontal text and a sesame in vertical text. If you give only a shape, the mark is filled. A string, such as "*", uses its first character as the mark, in the font of the text. If that font has no such character, the text has no marks.

image.alt: Two rows of five Chinese characters, each with a small mark over it. The first row has filled marks: dot, circle, double circle, triangle and sesame. The second row has the same marks open.

info.p: text-emphasis sets the style and the color together. The marks have the size of half the font, and the line grows to make room for them when its line-height leaves none.

text-emphasis-position chooses the side of the text. In horizontal text, over is above the characters and under is below them. In vertical lines, right is on the right of the characters and left is on the left. The initial value, over right, puts the marks above horizontal text and on the right of vertical text. text-emphasis-color sets the color, which is the color of the text when you do not set it:

step.cmd: Leave some characters without a mark

info.p: By default, spaces and punctuation get no mark. text-emphasis-skip lists the kinds of characters to skip: spaces, punctuation, symbols and narrow, the characters that are not wide or full-width, such as the Latin letters in a line of Japanese text. This example marks the punctuation too:

text-shadow takes a list of shadows. Each one has a horizontal and a vertical offset, then an optional blur, an optional spread and a color. Use a font that you embed with @font-face, as explains, when the shadow has a blur:

The offsets are on the page, whatever the writing mode: a positive horizontal offset moves the shadow to the right, and a positive vertical offset moves it down. The blur softens the edge of the shadow. The spread makes the shadow thicker by that length on all sides. The color is the color of the text when you leave it out.
With several shadows, separated by commas, the first one is on top:
The shadow also has the underlines, overlines and lines through the text of the element.

step.cmd: Draw a shadow inside the letters

info.p: In a font that you embed with @font-face, write inset before the lengths of a shadow to draw it inside the letters, as if they were cut into the page:

result.p: The text of your document has marks and shadows in horizontal and vertical lines.
